Surya Namaskar, or Sun Salutation, is a sequence of 12 powerful yoga asanas [PROG_Y_001]. It is best performed early morning on an empty stomach [PROG_Y_001]. 

Ek complete round consists of two sets, starting with the right leg and then the left [PROG_Y_001]. Each posture is coordinated with your breath, making it a very calming practice [PROG_Y_001].

Anulom Vilom ek powerful pranayama hai jo mind ko calm karta hai aur stress ko relieve karta hai [PROG_P_001]. Iske aur bhi fayde hain:

- Yeh body mein Tridoshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) ko balance karne mein help karta hai [PROG_P_001].
- Yeh patience aur concentration ko improve karta hai [PROG_P_001].

Start karne ke liye, comfortable meditative pose mein baith kar spine straight rakhein, aur 5-10 rounds se start karein [PROG_P_001]. Iska best time subah (morning) breakfast se pehle hota hai [PROG_P_001]. Contraindications: Agar aapko cold, cough, ya fever hai toh ise practice na karein [PROG_P_001].

Ek healthy lifestyle ke liye balanced diet zaroori hai. Breakfast mein fried foods ki jagah poha, upma, ya idli le sakte hain [PROG_D_001]. 

Lunch mein 2 rotis, ek bowl dal, sabzi aur salad khaayein [PROG_D_001]. Dinner sabse halka hona chahiye, jisme khichdi ya dal ke sath vegetable stir-fry ek accha option hai [PROG_D_001]. 

Din bhar mein kam se kam 8-10 glasses of paani (water) piyein aur processed sugar serta excessive salt se bachein [PROG_D_001]. Cravings ke liye nuts and seeds se snacking karna behtar hai [PROG_D_001].

Kapalbhati, or Skull Shining Breath, is an invigorating pranayama that cleanses the body through active, forceful exhalation and passive inhalation [PROG_P_002]. Sit comfortably with a straight spine, take a deep breath in, and exhale in short, powerful bursts while your stomach pumps inwards [PROG_P_002]. 

Start with a round of 20-30 pumps and do up to 3 rounds with breaks [PROG_P_002]. Practice it on an empty stomach, preferably in the morning [PROG_P_002]. It stimulates the digestive system, improves metabolic rate, and aids in weight loss [PROG_P_002]. 

Avoid Kapalbhati if you are pregnant, have high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia, or epilepsy [PROG_P_002].

Trikonasana, or Triangle Pose, is a foundational standing pose that stretches the entire body [PROG_Y_003]. To do it, stand with your feet wide apart, turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot in slightly, extend your torso to the right, and place your right hand on your shin, ankle, or the floor while extending your left arm up [PROG_Y_003]. 

It stretches the hamstrings, hips, and spine, strengthens the legs and core, is therapeutic for stress, and improves digestion [PROG_Y_003]. Avoid this pose if you have a headache, low blood pressure, or a neck injury, and do not lock your knees [PROG_Y_003]. Hold for 30-60 seconds [PROG_Y_003].

Garmi ke liye aap Sheetali Pranayama (Cooling Breath) kar sakte hain [PROG_P_004]. 

Comfortable baith kar apni tongue ko tube shape mein roll karke mouth se bahar nikaalein [PROG_P_004]. Tube ke through slow aur deep inhale karein, phir tongue ko andar karke mouth close karein aur nostrils ke through slow exhale karein [PROG_P_004]. Isko 5-10 times repeat karein [PROG_P_004]. 

Yeh body ko cool karta hai, mental aur emotional excitation reduce karta hai, aur hunger aur thirst ko control karne mein help karta hai [PROG_P_004]. Low blood pressure ya respiratory issues jaise asthma wale logon ke liye yeh recommended nahi hai [PROG_P_004]. Clean environment mein practice karein [PROG_P_004].

Immunity badhane ke liye ek balanced diet zaroori hai [PROG_D_002]. Citrus fruits jaise amla, oranges, aur lemons Vitamin C ke ache source hain jo immunity boost karte hain [PROG_D_002]. Turmeric (haldi) mein curcumin hota hai, jo ek powerful anti-inflammatory compound hai; ise milk ya curries mein add karein [PROG_D_002]. Ginger aur garlic bhi medicinal properties ke liye acche hain [PROG_D_002]. 

Yogurt gut health ke liye probiotics ka great source hai [PROG_D_002]. Green leafy vegetables jaise spinach (palak) antioxidants se packed hain, aur almonds Vitamin E ka great source hain [PROG_D_002].

Yogi Devvrat is a certified RYT 500 Yoga Alliance instructor with over 15 years of experience, having started his journey in Rishikesh under traditional yoga gurus [PROG_I_001]. His teaching style blends classical Hatha yoga with modern Vinyasa flow, focusing on alignment, breath, pranayama, and meditation [PROG_I_001]. He specializes in therapeutic yoga to help manage chronic pain and stress-related ailments [PROG_I_001].

Millets are ancient grains that are gluten-free and rich in fiber, protein, and antioxidants [PROG_D_004]. They have a low glycemic index, making them suitable for diabetics, and high fiber content that helps keep you full for longer, aiding in weight management [PROG_D_004]. Specific varieties include Ragi (Finger Millet) for calcium and bone health, Jowar (Sorghum) for iron and protein, and Bajra (Pearl Millet) for magnesium and heart health [PROG_D_004]. You can easily add them to your diet by swapping rice with millet or making rotis from their flour [PROG_D_004].

You can practice Shavasana (Corpse Pose) by lying flat on your back with your feet apart and arms by your sides, palms facing up. Close your eyes, let go of breath control, and release tension (*thakaan*). Spend 5-10 minutes to help reduce blood pressure, calm the nervous system, and combat insomnia [PROG_Y_004]. 

Alternatively, try Balasana (Childs Pose) by kneeling, sitting back on your heels, and folding forward with your forehead on the floor. Hold for 30 seconds to a few minutes with deep breathing to stretch the body, relieve back and neck pain, and alleviate stress and fatigue [PROG_Y_005].

Dia Malik is a certified clinical nutritionist with a Masters degree in Food and Nutrition [PROG_I_002]. She has helped over 500 clients achieve goals like weight management, PCOS, and diabetes through diet [PROG_I_002]. 

Her philosophy is focused on a no-deprivation approach, creating sustainable diet plans that fit your lifestyle and cultural eating habits [PROG_I_002]. You can book a one-on-one consultation with her to create a khaane ka plan (eating plan) that works for you [PROG_I_002]. She is available on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4 PM to 6 PM [PROG_I_002].

Staying hydrated is crucial for overall health as water regulates body temperature, lubricates joints, and delivers nutrients to cells [PROG_D_003]. Aim for 8-10 glasses of water per day, and sip it throughout the day to boost physical and mental performance [PROG_D_003]. Drinking water before meals can aid in weight management, and it is essential for kidney function and flushing out toxins [PROG_D_003].
